ghi: THAM KHẢO — không phải chấm đạt; chủ dự án chấm cuối (§13.4)

tra_loi.Q1: Britain. A British flag (Union Jack) is raised on the tower of the town in frames 22-25, 4-5 Aug 1704, after a fleet attacks the Rock. The caption 'The Rock changes hands' appears just before. The pictures don't show who held it before.
tra_loi.Q2: 'The Great Siege' (caption 20 Jun 1779). A line of wooden works and trenches is built on the flat land facing the Rock, with cannon fire and smoke. Ships blockade the bay.
tra_loi.Q3: The town is cut off. Ships blockade the bay and a siege line stands on land, so supplies can't reach it. Frames 52-53 show a man and woman picking plants on the hillside, which suggests they are short of food. Frames 60-61 show the town burning at night, apparently under bombardment (Apr 1781). I can't tell for certain that hunger is the cause, but it looks like a blockade.
tra_loi.Q4: A fleet of ships with red flags (British) arrives in the bay (27 Jan 1780, and again later). It looks like a relief convoy. Not completely sure.
tra_loi.Q5: A big attack in Sept 1782. A line of ships sails in on 12-13 Sep, with cannon smoke from the land works on 8 Sep. Then on the night of 13-14 Sep a row of ships near the Rock burns and glows in the dark. It looks like the attacking fleet is destroyed by fire.
tra_loi.Q6: Fields and farms first appear (1789-1900s), then houses and streets (1910). A runway is built on the sand in 1939, and ships and an airfield follow in the 1940s. Later come apartment blocks and a dense modern town (2026), with the border crossing, airport and roads.
tra_loi.Q7: On 8 Jun 1969 a crowd of people stands at the border gate, and the frontier appears to be closed or blocked (the gate is shown with people in front of it). Later, in the 1970s and 80s, the area fills with buildings and trees, and the border town grows. I'm not sure exactly what happens at the gate.
tra_loi.Q8: The runway and a crossing. In 2026 there are people walking on a street and across the airstrip/crosswalk at the border. The two built-up towns face each other across the open runway, with people crossing on foot between them. It looks like daily commuter traffic.

lac.why: Jumps from the modern day to 1411 and 1704 with burning town and no explanation.
Flash-forward to 1782 ships burning at the start, with no context.
1729 and 2015 are shown in quick succession, and the timeline jumps around.
The caption jumps back to Jan 1705, then Feb 1727, so the order is confusing.
Two people on a hillside picking plants, with no caption saying why.
A chain of yellow rings on the water has no explanation.
Faceless figures in a 1910 street, with no clear link to the story.
A 1969 gate and crowd with no text, so what happens at the border is unclear.
Many shots of the 2026 town, with no narrative.

tra_loi.Q1: Britain. After the August 1704 attack from the sea, a Union Jack (British flag) is raised on the tower at the town wall (frames 22-25). The townspeople leave on foot with donkeys and bundles (frames 26-29).
tra_loi.Q2: A siege. The chapter title reads '1779 — The Great Siege'. Wooden entrenchments and camps are built on the sandy land north of the rock, and cannon smoke follows (frames 47-51).
tra_loi.Q3: Not sure of the cause from the pictures alone. Ships blockade the bay in 1779-1780 and the town is cut off by sea (frames 49-57). A man and woman pick plants on the hillside in Jan 1780 (frames 52-53), which suggests a food shortage. The video shows no text about hunger.
tra_loi.Q4: Ships. Fleets of sailing ships with red flags arrive in the bay (frames 55-58, Jan 1780). Later scenes show ships near the town in 1781 (frame 59), but the pictures don't say whether they carry help.
tra_loi.Q5: A sea battle with burning ships. In Sep 1782 a line of floating batteries or ships lies off the rock (frames 76-85). At night on 13-14 Sep the ships burn in a row in front of the rock (frames 86-88). Cannon fire and smoke on 8 Sep come first (frames 73-75).
tra_loi.Q6: Fields and farmland first, then houses and streets. A fence or wall is built in 1729-1734 (frames 39-43). Fields appear after the siege (frames 96-117). A neighbourhood grows from 1904 (frame 113). An airstrip or runway is built in 1939 (chapter title, frame 118) and extended into the sea around 1942-43 (frames 139-145). By 2026 there is a dense modern town with tower blocks and an airport (frames 152-166).
tra_loi.Q7: Not sure what it is. On 8 Jun 1969 a crowd of people stands near the border area (frame 151). Afterwards, from 1973 to 1984, the land fills with buildings and trees (frames 149-153). Nothing on screen reads as a gate closing or opening.
tra_loi.Q8: Not sure. The pictures show a continuous built-up area with a border strip and an airstrip between the rock's town and the modern town to the north (frames 155-168). In 2026, people walk along a street and cross a road or zebra crossing at the airstrip (frames 1, 158-159). So it looks as if people cross the border on foot.

lac.why: Jumps from the 2026 opening to 1411 and 1704 with no explanation.
A 1782 night flash-forward appears before the story reaches it.
The 1939, 1943 and 2026 montage comes before the 1704 chapter title.
Frames jump among 1729, 2015, 1705, 1727 and 1731 with no clear order.
A man and woman gather plants, and the picture doesn't say why.
A town burns on 14 Apr 1781, and the picture doesn't say who is attacking.
The 1782 scenes show trenches with no explanation.
A street in 1910 with stick-figure people has no obvious point.
The 1969 crowd isn't explained; there is no visible gate or caption.
The ending flashes between 2026, 1735, 1943 and 1731 with no clear sequence.

tra_loi.Q1: Britain. A British flag (Union Jack) is raised over the tower and walls on 4–5 Aug 1704 after ships bombard the town. The chapter title reads '1704 — The Rock changes hands', and the Spanish civilians then walk away across the plain. That sequence suggests the Rock passed from Spain to Britain, but no Spanish flag is shown.
tra_loi.Q2: A siege. The chapter card '1779 — The Great Siege' appears on 20 Jun 1779. It shows a long wall or fortification line on the sandy land, trenches, tents and camps, and smoke or fire.
tra_loi.Q3: The town is cut off by a siege and blockade. Ships ring the bay, and the pictures suggest food runs short. A couple forage for wild plants on the hillside in Jan 1780. There are fires in the town in Apr 1781, and the ruined town appears in 1781–82. Hunger is only implied; no food or starvation is shown directly.
tra_loi.Q4: Ships. A relief fleet with red ensigns arrives on 27 Jan 1780 and sails into the bay, and the supply convoy then sits in front of the town. I am not sure whether later arrivals are also relief.
tra_loi.Q5: A naval battle. On 12–13 Sep 1782 a line of ships approaches the Rock. At night on 13–14 Sep the ships burn in a row off the Rock, so a fleet attack is destroyed by fire. Before that, a bombardment with smoke and fires on 8 Sep. The pictures do not show who wins.
tra_loi.Q6: Over the centuries the sandy land first has a wall or fortification line (1729–1734), then fields and farms (1789–1900s) and a few houses, then a street and a small settlement (1904–1910). An airstrip or runway is built in 1939 (chapter card 'A runway on the sand') and extended in the 1940s, with a few buildings beside it. Later, from the 1970s on, housing and apartment blocks fill in, and by 2026 a dense town covers the land, with the runway in the 2026 scenes.
tra_loi.Q7: In June 1969 (8 Jun, 15:09) a crowd of people gathers at the gate and the border appears to close, since the land looks empty before and after. From 1969 on, the land beside the border is built up, with apartment blocks by 1980 and 1984. Whether the gate stays closed or reopens is not shown.
tra_loi.Q8: Not sure. The pictures show two dense towns facing each other across a road or an airfield, with pedestrians walking across a crossing (frame 1) and a street. This suggests a shared border crossing or road, but nothing shows what links them.

lac.why: The film opens in 2026 with no explanation, and the cut to 1411 and 1704 is jarring.
A Sep 1782 flash-forward appears before the 1704 story and is unexplained.
A column of people walks away from the Rock, and it is unclear who they are or why they leave.
Time jumps around: 1729, 2015, then Jan 1705 and Feb 1727, with no clear order.
A couple picking plants is the only hint of hunger, and no text confirms it.
A night fire in the town gives no clear cause or story link.
The floating line of rafts or batteries and the ship formations are not clearly explained, and the battle result is unclear.
A cannon flash on 14 Feb 1810 and the 1811–1857 ship scenes have no clear story.
Street scenes in 1910 with stick figures do not connect to the story.
The 1940–43 ship and town shots show the war context without text or story.
The 1969 crowd at the gate is shown without any sign of what happens.
A street with pedestrians in 2026, and the repeated 2026 town shots from frame 155 onward, do not show a link between the two towns.
Dated 2026 shots mixed with 1735, 1943 and 1731 give a confusing timeline in the closing montage.
